A <b>AWS CLI</b> é um programa que você: The AWS CLI is a program you install on your computer to talk to AWS by typing, instead of clicking around the website. Everything you can do in the console (create a server, upload a file, create a user) you can do with a command — and the command is always aws .
A <b>VPC</b> é a sua rede privada na AWS: The VPC is your private network on AWS. Create one with the block 10.0.0.0/16. (VPC commands live inside aws ec2)
A <b>ana</b> precisa de um acesso tempor: ana needs temporary access that applies to nobody else on the team. Creating a managed policy for this pollutes the account: write an inline policy called acesso-temp, which lives inside her and goes away with her.
A <b>fila</b> guarda tarefas pra serem p: A queue holds tasks to be processed later — the order goes into the queue and someone processes it in their own time. Start by listing the account's queues.

AWS CLI (simulator) — general manual
====================================

USAGE
    aws <serviço> <comando> [opções]

AVAILABLE SERVICES
    s3          Object storage — high-level commands (mb, cp, ls, sync...)
    s3api       Low-level S3 operations (versioning, policies...)
    ec2         Virtual machines (instances, security groups, key pairs)
    iam         Users, groups, roles and permissions
    lambda      Serverless functions
    dynamodb    NoSQL database
    sqs         Message queues
    sns         Notifications (pub/sub)
    apigateway  Managed HTTP APIs
    route53     DNS and domains
    cloudfront  CDN (edge caching)
    ecr         Container image registry
    ecs         Run containers (clusters, tasks, services)
    secretsmanager  Passwords and secrets
    stepfunctions   Step orchestration (workflows)
    events      EventBridge: events and schedules
    eks         Managed Kubernetes
    glue        Data catalog (and crawlers)
    athena      SQL straight on S3 files
    kms         Encryption keys
    cloudtrail  Auditing: who did what in the account
    ssm         Systems Manager (Parameter Store)
    cognito-idp User login (user pools)
    autoscaling Automatic elasticity
    sts         Session identity (get-caller-identity)

MANUALS
    aws <serviço> help                e.g.: aws s3 help
    aws <serviço> <comando> help      e.g.: aws s3 mb help

OPTIONS THAT WORK WITH ANY COMMAND
    --query '<expressão>'   filters/transforms the output (JMESPath).
                            E.g.: --query 'Policies[*].Arn'
    --output <formato>      json (default) or text.
    command > file          redirects the output to a file (saves it).
                            E.g.: ... get-policy-version ... > lab_policy.json

TERMINAL UTILITIES
    ls            lists the files (fictional ones + the ones you created with '>')
    cat <arq>     shows a file's contents
    clear         clears the screen
    help          this manual

Analisar grandes volumes de dados que já: Analyzing large volumes of data already in S3 without building infrastructure: logs, exports, sales data. Ideal for one-off questions (\"how many sales per region this month?\") without paying for a database that's always on.
Analisar texto em escala: medir a satisf: Analyzing text at scale: measuring satisfaction across thousands of reviews, classifying support tickets, extracting information from documents. What a human would do by reading, it does in bulk.

Antes da reunião de custo, compare lado: Before the cost meeting, compare api-loja-build and app-mobile-build side by side: each one's machine and timeout.
Antes da reunião de mudanças, liste os c: Before the change meeting, list the pending change sets of pedidos-dev.
Antes de agrupar o custo, às vezes você: Before grouping cost, sometimes you just want to know which values exist in a dimension. List the values of the SERVICE dimension.
Antes de analisar sentimento você precis: Before analyzing sentiment you need to know the language — and Comprehend figures it out on its own. Detect the dominant language of a text.
Antes de apagar um apelido, confira quan: Before deleting an alias, check how many the reports key has. List only its aliases.
Antes de apagar, confirme que o <b>loja-: Before deleting, confirm that loja-tg really is there — and grab its ARN.
Antes de aprovar, a tech lead quer ver o: Before approving, the tech lead wants to see the vacation screen's pull request in full: branches, commits and whether it was already merged.
Antes de avisar o time, confira que o re: Before telling the team, check that www's A record really is in the zone.
Antes de baixar uma política, você preci: Before downloading a policy, you need to know which version is active. Check the metadata of lab_policy (DefaultVersionId shows up there).
Antes de confiar num scanner, confirme q: Before trusting a scanner, confirm it's active. See Inspector's status on the account.
Antes de configurar, o time quer entende: Before configuring, the team wants to understand the pace options: update one machine at a time, half or all together. List the deploy configurations that exist.
Antes de criar mais um, dê uma olhada em: Before creating another one, take a look at all your buckets.
Antes de criar qualquer coisa, veja o qu: Before creating anything, see what exists: list your EC2 instances.
Antes de criar uma política de cache pró: Before creating your own cache policy, see whether someone already did. List only the custom ones.
Antes de desligar qualquer coisa, descub: Before turning anything off, find out the obvious: is /api/erros being dumped somewhere? List its subscriptions.
Antes de dizer na reunião que o custo va: Before saying in the meeting that the cost will go down, confirm the rule is in effect. (an empty response means nothing is being moved — everything stays in the expensive class)
Antes de escolher o IP fixo de um servid: Before picking the fixed IP for a new server, see which private IPs are already taken on the network interfaces.
Antes de escolher um modelo, veja o que: Before picking a model, see what it supports (text? image? streaming response?). Fetch the details of the model amazon.titan-text-express-v1.
Antes de escrever script, veja o que a A: Before writing a script, see what AWS already ships ready-made. List the available documents and notice they're split into two types that don't mix: Command and Automation.
Antes de fazer rollback você precisa sab: Before rolling back you need to know where to go back to. List the versions of processa-pedido.
Antes de fechar o chamado, liste os addo: Before closing the ticket, list the addons of cluster-k8s and confirm that both you installed show up.
Antes de fechar o relatório de custo, co: Before closing the cost report, check what's tagged on the queue pagamentos-cartao.
Antes de guardar arquivo importante no <: Before storing an important file in bucket-via-api, check whether it has versioning. Notice what comes back when versioning was never turned on.
Antes de ir pra produção, monte a rede d: Before going to production, set up the staging network: VPC 10.40.0.0/16.
Antes de ir pra produção, o time quer te: Before going to production, the team wants to test on a copy. Create the environment loja-homolog in the same application, with the same platform.
Antes de liberar a <b>ana</b> pra mexer: Before clearing ana to touch production, answer without testing in production: can she read and can she delete an object in S3? Simulate both actions at once.
Antes de ligar a aplicação de verdade, t: Before turning on the real application, test the write path: write the line deploy-concluido to the stream servidor-01 of /frota/web. (the timestamp is in milliseconds since 1970 — in the terminal it would be $(date +%s)000)
Antes de ligar o CI, confirme que o <b>b: Before turning on CI, confirm that buildspec.yml is on main of portal-rh — and look at its size (fileSize).
Antes de ligar o app mobile, confira que: Before turning on the mobile app, check that the policy of processa-pedido has both permissions: S3's and API Gateway's.
Antes de ligar uma aplicação nova nele,: Before hooking a new application to it, find out where logs-aplicacao lives. (transfer between regions costs, and latency from the other side of the world shows up in the response time)
Antes de mandar a mensagem \\\"pode puxa: Before sending the \"go ahead and pull\" message to staging, check that the policy on loja-imagens really is there.
Antes de mexer em alarme, veja o que já: Before touching alarms, see what's already being extracted from /climb/app. List the group's metric filters.
Antes de mexer em qualquer coisa numa co: Before touching anything in an account that isn't yours, the first question is: who am I here? Look at the details of the user ana — and notice that, without giving the name, the same command answers who is calling.
Antes de mexer em qualquer coisa, veja o: Before touching anything, see what the recipe migracao-banco declares: image, memory, ports. Each registration is an immutable revision — you never edit, you always register a new one.
Antes de mexer na <b>acesso-s3</b>, desc: Before touching acesso-s3, find out in how many places it's attached.
Antes de mexer na máquina, veja só os di: Before touching the machine, look only at the disks attached to it, instead of all of the account's.
Antes de mexer no GitHub Enterprise, vej: Before touching GitHub Enterprise, see which connections depend on it: list the connections filtering by the host ghe-empresa, and check the host list.
Antes de mexer no repositório do time de: Before touching the payments team's repository, look at what already lives in it. List the details of pagamentos/checkout-api and answer for yourself: is there any image in there that nobody knows where it came from?
Antes de mexer no webhook, veja se dá pr: Before touching the webhook, see whether you can roll back: list the versions of webhook-pagamento. (if only $LATEST comes back, no rollback is possible — it's time to publish one)
Antes de montar um app multilíngue, veja: Before building a multilingual app, see which languages Translate supports.
Antes de o script de backup rodar à meia: Before the backup script runs at midnight, test in the cheapest way possible whether the bucket contratos-2026 exists and whether you have access.
Antes de rodar banco no cluster, veja qu: Before running a database on the cluster, see which managed addons cluster-k8s already has.
Antes de rodar um contêiner na AWS, a <b: Before running a container on AWS, its image needs to be stored somewhere — that place is ECR. Start by listing the repositories.
Antes de sair mexendo, registre o tráfeg: Before you start changing things, record the traffic. Create the bucket flowlogs-loja and enable a flow log on the lab's VPC capturing ALL. (get the VPC id with aws ec2 describe-vpcs)
Antes de sintetizar, confira o que a con: Before synthesizing, check what the account has. List the lexicons in this region. (lexicons are per region: what exists in São Paulo doesn't exist in Virginia)
Antes de subir o servidor web na rede <b: Before launching the web server on the network 10.20.0.0/16, confirm it has an internet gateway attached. Filter the gateways by VPC.
Antes de subir qualquer coisa, <b>liste: Before bringing anything up, list the subnet groups — that's how you find out whether someone left a public subnet in the mix.
Antes de subir qualquer coisa, a pergunt: Before launching anything, the basic question: which regions can the account operate in? (a forgotten resource in a region nobody looks at is a classic — and this list is how you sweep for it)
Antes de subir, confira o que o template: Before launching, check what the template requires: validate pedidos-api.yaml and look at the Parameters (with each one's default value).
Antes de tentar entrar no container, con: Before trying to get into the container, confirm whether the migration task was born with exec turned on — otherwise you'll lose ten minutes on an error that can't be fixed. Describe the task and look for the field enableExecuteCommand.
Antes de testar de novo, confirme que a: Before testing again, confirm that the route 0.0.0.0/0 showed up in the subnet's table.
Antes de tudo: instalar e configurar a C: First of all: install and configure the CLI. It's the everyday tool.

THE ONES THAT MATTER
    VisibilityTimeout            how long the consumer has to
                                 process before the message comes back
    ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds  long polling (up to 20): receive
                                 waits for the message instead of answering
                                 empty — cuts needlessly charged requests
    MessageRetentionPeriod       how long the message survives in the
                                 queue (default 4 days, max 14)
    DelaySeconds                 delays delivery of every new message
    RedrivePolicy                turns on the dead-letter queue (DLQ)

It only works if the destination hasn't moved since the source branched off it; if

ONLY WHAT CHANGED
    Running it again sends nothing: sync compares source and destination and
    sends only what's new or changed. It also works s3:// → s3:// and
    s3:// → local folder.

--delete
    Deletes from the destination what no longer exists in the source (mirror). Without
    it, the file you removed from the folder stays in the bucket.
    Mind the order: sync <source> <destination>. Swapped, 
    --delete wipes what you wanted to keep.

ETag — THE LOCK

EXAMPLE

The JSON uses DynamoDB's format: each value declares its type

aws dynamodb query\\n\\nUSO\\n aws dy:
aws dynamodb query

USAGE
    aws dynamodb query --table-name PedidosCliente \
        --key-condition-expression "cliente = :c" \
        --expression-attribute-values '{":c":{"S":"ana"}}'

    aws dynamodb query --table-name PedidosCliente \
        --key-condition-expression "cliente = :c AND #d > :d" \
        --expression-attribute-names '{"#d":"data"}' \
        --expression-attribute-values '{":c":{"S":"ana"},":d":{"S":"2026-07-10"}}'

DynamoDB's most important operation. It goes STRAIGHT to the partition and reads only
what matters — unlike scan, which reads the whole table and discards the rest.

RULES:
  - the condition ALWAYS starts with the partition key, with equality (=)
  - on the sort key these work: =, <, >, <=, >= and begins_with(field, :x)
  - you can't filter by a regular field: that's scan (or an index)
  - --scan-index-forward false reverses the order

The values don't go in the expression: they go in --expression-attribute-values,
referenced by :placeholder.

RESERVED WORD: data, status, name, date, count, type, user... are
DynamoDB reserved words and can't appear bare in the expression. Use a
placeholder #x and say who it is in --expression-attribute-names '{"#x":"data"}'.

USAGE
    aws logs start-query --log-group-name /climb/app \
        --start-time 0 --end-time 9999999999 \
        --query-string 'fields @timestamp, @message | filter level = "ERROR" | limit 20'

Runs a query with a QUERY LANGUAGE. Stages are separated by | and
applied in order:
    fields a, b        picks the columns (@timestamp and @message always exist)
    filter <expr>      field = "value", != , > , < , field like /text/
                       joined by and / or
    stats <f> by <c>   aggregates: count(), count(c), avg(c), sum(c), min(c), max(c)

    sort <col> [desc]  sorts
    limit N            cuts

you narrow the period and filter early — filtering at the end costs the same.
